title: `--userns=keep-id` does not override image `USER` as documented
body:
### Issue Description

When running an image that defines a `USER`, `podman run --userns=keep-id` keeps using the image-defined user instead of running the container process as the invoking host user.

This appears to contradict the Podman documentation for `keep-id`, which states that the container init process runs with the current user's UID and that this overrides the image's `USER` instruction unless `--user` is explicitly specified [[reference](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/main/docs/source/markdown/options/userns.container.md?plain=1#L63)].

I first noticed this behavior with Podman 5.8.4, but I can reproduce it with a source build of `main` as reported in the dedicated section below.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create an image defining a non-standard user, e.g.
```
$ cat Containerfile
FROM fedora:43
RUN useradd --uid 1001 appuser 
USER 1001

$ podman build -t user-override .
STEP 1/3: FROM fedora:43
STEP 2/3: RUN useradd --uid 1001 appuser 
--> cb69dcfa699f
STEP 3/3: USER 1001
COMMIT user-override
--> 812e937fa17e
Successfully tagged localhost/user-override:latest
812e937fa17ed7db783ff5eadfe6c9eedcf04842b655498d7ad850927d61142d
```
2. Run the image with a rootless user that has a different host uid from the one set in the Containerfile, and use `--userns=keep-id`
```
$ id
uid=1000(amadonna) gid=1000(amadonna) groups=1000(amadonna),...
$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id localhost/user-override:latest id
```

### Describe the results you received

With no options, the container runs as the `USER` from the Containerfile, as expected
```
$ podman run --rm localhost/user-override:latest id
uid=1001(appuser) gid=1001(appuser) groups=1001(appuser)
```

With the `--userns=keep-id` option, the Containerfile `USER` still wins (auxiliary groups are modified though)
```
$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id localhost/user-override:latest id
uid=1001(appuser) gid=1001(appuser) groups=1001(appuser),1000(amadonna)
```

### Describe the results you expected

A similar behavior as when there is no specific user entered in the Containerfile, e.g.:
```
$ podman run --rm fedora:43 id
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)

$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id fedora:43 id
uid=1000(amadonna) gid=1000(amadonna) groups=1000(amadonna)
```

Reusing the earlier example:
```
$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id localhost/user-override:latest id
uid=1000(amadonna) gid=1000(amadonna) groups=1000(amadonna)
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Additional environment details

### Additional information

I used an LLM to survey the Podman source code in relation to this behavior and here is a summary of its analysis:

> The likely cause is the interaction between these two code paths:
> 
> * `pkg/specgen/generate/container.go`: `CompleteSpec()` copies `inspectData.Config.User` into `s.User` when `s.User` is empty.
> * `pkg/specgen/generate/namespaces.go`: the `specgen.KeepID` handling only applies the invoking user's UID/GID when `s.User == ""`.
> 
> By the time the `keep-id` logic runs, `s.User` may already contain the image's `Config.User`, so the code can no longer distinguish an image-provided `USER` from an explicitly supplied `--user`. As a result, the image user prevents the `keep-id` process-user override from being applied.
> 
> The relevant condition appears to be the `if s.User == ""` check in the `specgen.KeepID` branch of `namespaceOptions()`. The intended condition seems to be whether the user was explicitly overridden by the caller, rather than whether the resolved `s.User` field is empty.
> 
> I verified that this code pattern is still present in Podman 6.1.0.
